oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is moclobemide; L3 human records show rapid oral absorption with Tmax about 1.44 h in normal subjects and 1.46 h in renally impaired subjects after single oral dosing, supporting absorption but not quantifying extent.

Close structural analog procainamide and its NAPA metabolite have measured absolute oral bioavailability values of 68–92%, with L2 context of 75–85% and acecainide 85%, all well above the 20% threshold.

L4 records show high fraction absorbed for related or similarly small oral drugs (NAPA 87–92%, levocetirizine ≥85%, bepotastine >85%, isoniazid Fa 0.97–0.99, rivaroxaban 80–100%), supporting favorable intestinal absorption.

L5 bidirectional permeability records show high permeability and low efflux for diverse compounds, including morpholine-amide-containing molecules, with no supplied record indicating significant gut-wall efflux or intestinal metabolism for the query or close analogs.

L6 hepatic clearance records are mixed and not moclobemide-specific: some morpholine-amide-containing compounds show low intrinsic clearance or good stability (C72, C77, C75, C73, C71), while others show moderate-to-high CLint (C70, C74, C78, C80); no direct moclobemide hepatic clearance measurement is supplied, so this does not provide affirmative evidence for F < 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for moclobemide itself was supplied; the decision relies on structural analogy to procainamide/NAPA, the physicochemical prior, and indirect exposure/absorption/permeability records.
No fed-state-specific moclobemide bioavailability or absorption record is available; the fed condition is not shown to reduce F below 20%.
L6 hepatic clearance records are for other molecules and are mixed; no direct moclobemide hepatic clearance or first-pass quantification is available.
No direct intestinal metabolism or gut-wall efflux measurement for moclobemide was supplied.
L3 direct moclobemide records provide only Tmax, not AUC/Cmax or F.
content.decision_summary: The query is moclobemide. L6 adds mixed hepatic clearance/metabolic-stability records for other molecules, with no direct moclobemide measurement; low-clearance records for some morpholine-amide-containing compounds are mechanistically supportive, while high-CLint records for other scaffolds are not transferable enough to overturn the prediction. Combined with L3 rapid absorption (Tmax ~1.4 h), L4 high fraction absorbed for related/small oral drugs, L5 high permeability/low efflux, and procainamide/NAPA absolute F 68–92%, the evidence supports F ≥ 20%. Confidence remains moderate because no direct moclobemide F or fed-state-specific measurement was supplied.
